# BigCatWise

> BigCatWise is a free, original educational website about big cats: the lion, tiger, leopard, jaguar, cheetah and snow leopard. It explains each species' appearance, behavior, habitat and range, and conservation status, with population estimates and facts sourced from the IUCN SSC Cat Specialist Group, the IUCN Red List, leading zoos, conservation organisations and peer reviewed research.

Content is general education. Population figures are estimates that change as new surveys are published.

## Species guides
- [Lion facts](https://bigcatwise.com/lion.html): Lion facts in plain English: how prides work, who does the hunting, where wild lions live today, how many are left and why the species is Vulnerable.
- [Tiger facts](https://bigcatwise.com/tiger.html): Tiger facts: the largest cat, why stripes are unique, where wild tigers survive, what they hunt and the latest IUCN population estimate.
- [Leopard facts](https://bigcatwise.com/leopard.html): Leopard facts: the most widespread big cat, how leopards hunt and cache prey in trees, what a black panther is, and why the leopard is Vulnerable.
- [Jaguar facts](https://bigcatwise.com/jaguar.html): Jaguar facts: the largest cat in the Americas, its skull piercing bite, love of water, rosettes with central spots, range and Near Threatened status.
- [Cheetah facts](https://bigcatwise.com/cheetah.html): Cheetah facts: how fast cheetahs really run, why they cannot roar, how they hunt by day, where they live and why only about 6,500 mature adults remain.
- [Snow leopard facts](https://bigcatwise.com/snow-leopard.html): Snow leopard facts: how this mountain cat survives at 3,000 to 5,000 m, why it cannot roar, what it eats, where it lives and how many remain.

## Topic guides
- [Big cat behavior](https://bigcatwise.com/behavior.html): How big cats behave: who lives in groups and who lives alone, how each species hunts, how they communicate by roaring and scent marking, and how cubs grow up.
- [Big cat habitats](https://bigcatwise.com/habitats.html): Where lions, tigers, leopards, jaguars, cheetahs and snow leopards live: continents, habitats from rainforest to 5,000 m mountains, and which species share ranges.
- [Big cat conservation](https://bigcatwise.com/conservation.html): Big cat conservation explained: IUCN Red List status for all six species, latest population estimates, the main threats, and the measures that actually help.
- [Big cat FAQ](https://bigcatwise.com/faq.html): Quick, sourced answers to common big cat questions: which cats count as big cats, the biggest and fastest, black panthers, white tigers, roaring and more.
- [Big cat glossary](https://bigcatwise.com/glossary.html): Plain English definitions of big cat terms: pride, coalition, rosette, melanism, flehmen response, IUCN Red List categories, CITES appendices and more.

## Tools
- [Which big cat is it? ID guide](https://bigcatwise.com/which-big-cat-is-it.html): Identify any big cat: leopard vs jaguar vs cheetah, snow leopard, tiger and lion compared side by side, plus a region by region guide to which big cats live where.
- [Big cats by region](https://bigcatwise.com/which-big-cat-is-it.html#by-region): deep links #africa, #asia, #south-asia, #southeast-asia, #east-asia, #central-asia, #middle-east, #americas (also #north-america, #central-america, #south-america), #elsewhere (also #europe, #australia)
- [Big cat comparison table](https://bigcatwise.com/compare.html): Compare lions, tigers, leopards, jaguars, cheetahs and snow leopards side by side: weight, length, range, habitat, social life, roaring, IUCN status and numbers.
- [Comparison table rows](https://bigcatwise.com/compare.html#table): deep links such as #row-tiger and #row-cheetah

## Blog
- [Which big cats can roar?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/which-big-cats-can-roar.html): Lions, tigers, leopards and jaguars can roar; snow leopards and cheetahs cannot. Here is what the anatomy research says about why, and what the others say instead.
- [Leopard vs jaguar vs cheetah](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/leopard-vs-jaguar-vs-cheetah.html): How to tell a leopard, jaguar and cheetah apart in seconds: location, spot pattern, build, face and behavior, with a side by side comparison table.
- [How fast is a cheetah?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/how-fast-is-a-cheetah.html): How fast cheetahs really run: 93 km/h measured in wild cheetahs, why most hunts are slower, how long a sprint lasts and what makes them so quick.
- [Why do tigers have stripes?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/why-do-tigers-have-stripes.html): Why tigers have stripes: camouflage for an ambush hunter, why an orange coat looks green to deer, and how unique stripe patterns let scientists count tigers.
- [How many big cats are left in the wild?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/how-many-big-cats-are-left.html): Latest estimates of how many lions, tigers, leopards, jaguars, cheetahs and snow leopards remain in the wild, what the numbers mean, and which is rarest.
- [Why do lions live in prides?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/why-do-lions-live-in-prides.html): Why lions live in groups when other big cats live alone: the field research on hunting, cub defence and territory, and what DNA revealed about pride kinship.
- [How big is a tiger's territory?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/how-big-is-a-tigers-territory.html): A tiger's territory can be 12 km² or more than 1,000 km². Radio collar studies from Russia, Thailand and Bangladesh show why prey decides the size.
- [Why do leopards drag their kills into trees?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/why-do-leopards-drag-their-kills-into-trees.html): Leopards hoist about half their kills into trees, mainly to stop hyenas stealing them. What a study of 2,032 kills in South Africa found.
- [What do snow leopards eat?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/what-do-snow-leopards-eat.html): Snow leopards mainly eat wild mountain goats and sheep, especially ibex and blue sheep of about 55 kg. What a review of 1,696 scats and a DNA study found.
- [Do jaguars hunt in water?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/do-jaguars-hunt-in-water.html): Yes. Jaguars swim and hunt fish, caiman and other aquatic prey. A Pantanal study found fish in 46% of scats and aquatic reptiles in 55%, with mammals only 11%.
- [Why do male lions have manes?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/why-do-male-lions-have-manes.html): A lion's mane is a signal: darker manes mark healthier, higher testosterone males that females prefer. Research on mane colour, heat costs and maneless lions.
- [Never enter a tiger enclosure: lessons from Yorkshire Wildlife Park](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/never-enter-a-tiger-enclosure.html): On 10 October 2026 a man died after entering the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park. What is known, why zoo barriers matter, and how tigers hunt.
- [Do cheetahs abandon hunts because they overheat?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/do-cheetahs-abandon-hunts-because-they-overheat.html): No: free-living cheetahs stop chases without overheating. Body temperature averaged 38.4 C at chase end; heat rises more after a kill than during the sprint.
- [Are tigers nocturnal?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/are-tigers-nocturnal.html): Mostly, but not strictly. Wild tigers are most active at night, dawn and dusk, track their prey's schedule, and turn more nocturnal where people are busy by day.
- [Can leopards live near people?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/can-leopards-live-near-people.html): Yes, to a striking degree. In India leopards live in dense farmland with no wild prey, eat mostly domestic animals, visit homes at night and rarely attack people.
- [Why do so few cheetah cubs survive?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/why-do-so-few-cheetah-cubs-survive.html): On the Serengeti Plains only about 1 in 20 cheetah cubs reached independence, mostly because lions and hyenas killed them. Elsewhere, survival can be far higher.
- [Why do snow leopards have such low genetic diversity?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/why-do-snow-leopards-have-low-genetic-diversity.html): Genome studies find snow leopards have the lowest genetic diversity of any big cat, mostly because their population has always been small. Here is what that means.
- [How often do lion hunts succeed?](https://bigcatwise.com/blog/how-often-do-lion-hunts-succeed.html): Most lion hunts fail. In one Namibian study lions made 156 kills from 920 attempts. Here is what raises their odds: teamwork, cover, prey choice and more.

## Games (free, no sign up, no personal data collected by us)
- [Games](https://bigcatwise.com/games/): Free big cat games that teach real facts: identify big cats by their coats, sprint like a cheetah and round up big cats by habitat. No sign up.
- [Rosette Detective](https://bigcatwise.com/games/rosette-detective/): Free big cat ID game: look at a close up of a coat and decide if it is a lion, tiger, leopard, jaguar, cheetah or snow leopard. Learn a real fact every round.
- [Cheetah Burst](https://bigcatwise.com/games/cheetah-burst/): Tap to sprint like a cheetah, turn when the prey swerves and catch it before you run out of energy. A free speed game based on real wild cheetah research.
- [Range Roundup](https://bigcatwise.com/games/range-roundup/): Free big cat habitat game: round up which lions, tigers, leopards, jaguars, cheetahs and snow leopards live wild in each region and habitat. Real facts every card.

## For teachers and students (free printables, lesson plans, research list)
- [Teachers](https://bigcatwise.com/teachers/): Free big cat teaching resources: printable fact sheets, worksheets with answer keys, vocabulary, NGSS aligned lesson ideas for K-12 and fact based classroom games.
- [Fact sheets](https://bigcatwise.com/teachers/big-cat-fact-sheets.html): Six free printable big cat fact sheets for the classroom: lion, tiger, leopard, jaguar, cheetah and snow leopard, each with sourced facts and a drawing space.
- [Worksheets](https://bigcatwise.com/teachers/big-cat-worksheets.html): Four free printable big cat worksheets: which big cat am I riddles, a habitat match, cheetah speed math and a lion research reading for older students.
- [Answer keys](https://bigcatwise.com/teachers/answer-keys.html): Answer keys for the free BigCatWise big cat worksheets: which big cat am I, habitat match, cheetah speed math and the lion pride research reading.
- [Vocabulary](https://bigcatwise.com/teachers/big-cat-vocabulary.html): A printable big cat vocabulary list for the classroom: 24 science words like adaptation, camouflage, pride, rosette and predator, with kid friendly definitions.
- [Big cat adaptations lesson plan](https://bigcatwise.com/teachers/big-cat-adaptations-lesson-plan.html): A free 45 minute big cat adaptations lesson plan for grades 3 to 5: structure and function cards, a camouflage investigation, exit ticket and NGSS 4-LS1-1 alignment.
- [Cheetah worksheet for 3rd grade](https://bigcatwise.com/teachers/cheetah-worksheet-3rd-grade.html): A free printable cheetah worksheet for 3rd grade: a short reading passage about the fastest land animal, comprehension questions, speed math and an answer key.
- [Lion pride lesson plan](https://bigcatwise.com/teachers/lion-pride-lesson-plan.html): A free grade 3 lesson plan on why some animals live in groups, using real lion pride research. Includes argument writing, a sorting activity and a high school extension.
- [Research](https://bigcatwise.com/research/): Peer reviewed big cat papers behind BigCatWise, grouped by topic with full references and DOIs checked on Crossref. A starting point for school reports.
